title: Remove i57 legacy filename fallback from generate-multipage-report.js
description:
After bd i57 Phase B shipped (df08e1e) and Phase A migrated mammoth-lakes (92cb9ce), the renderer still carries a temporary legacy-name fallback in template/reports/multipage/lib/load-research.js. Remove the fallback once: (1) all 6 active clients have canonical pagespeed-data.json, ga4-data.json, search-console.json, keyword-research.json (or have those data sources legitimately absent rather than under legacy names); (2) at least matt-wallmow plus 5 other clients render with zero fallback warnings under a fresh /seo-audit run.

Removal scope: delete template/reports/multipage/lib/load-research.js + tests + fixtures, revert the 6 wire-in sites in generate-multipage-report.js to direct fs.existsSync/JSON.parse calls. Cross-reference commit df08e1e for the exact wiring.

title: build_audit.py reads search-console-pages.json which nothing writes
description:
platform/scripts/build_audit.py:336 calls _load_research_file('search-console-pages.json') and line 575 calls _load_research_file('search-console-query-pages.json'). No code in the repo writes either filename — current Python and JS pipelines write either gsc-pages.json/gsc-queries.json (legacy) or search-console.json (canonical). These reads silently return None and the analyzers downstream skip their work without error.

Surfaced during bd i57 Phase A archaeology. Latent for an unknown duration. Fix by routing through a load_research_json(canonical, legacy) helper that prefers search-console.json and falls back to the gsc-* split files. Out of i57 scope because no canonical writer for split GSC currently exists; this is a Python-side reader bug.

title: Renderer-vs-pipeline filename mismatch leaves Python-pipeline research invisible
description:
The multipage renderer (template/reports/multipage/generate-multipage-report.js) reads research files using the JS-gather naming convention only. The Python build_audit.py pipeline writes files under different names, so client research collected via the Python path is silently invisible to the renderer.

Concrete name pairs (renderer-name / Python-pipeline-name):
- pagespeed-data.json / pagespeed.json + pagespeed-interior.json
- ga4-data.json / ga4-acquisition.json + ga4-devices.json + ga4-landing-pages.json + ga4-page-performance.json
- search-console.json / gsc-pages.json + gsc-queries.json + gsc-devices.json + gsc-query-pages.json
- keyword-research.json / keyword-suggestions.json
- (no JS analog) / crux.json, brand-mentions.json, social-audit.json, client-rankings.json, competitor-domain-metrics.json, competitor-domains.json, competitor-pagespeed.json, competitor-serp-comparison.json, serp-results.json

Concrete current-state evidence (Phase E close-out 2026-05-05):
- mammoth-lakes seo/research/ has 30 JSON files, mostly Python-pipeline names. Render log warns: lighthouseResults empty, coreWebVitals missing, contentQuality missing, internalLinking.totalPages missing. Underlying data exists in pagespeed.json + crawl-data.json + ga4-*/gsc-* but the renderer asks for pagespeed-data.json + ga4-data.json + search-console.json and finds nothing.
- p3realtync has hybrid: client-info.json, ga4-data.json, rank-history.json, search-console.json (renderer-style names) AND pagespeed.json (Python-style). Renderer picks up the renderer-style ones, misses pagespeed.

Two viable directions (decide before fixing):
A) Unify producer side: have build_audit.py emit consolidated files matching renderer naming (single ga4-data.json, single search-console.json, pagespeed-data.json with same shape as JS gather). Lets the renderer stay simple.
B) Unify consumer side: extend the renderer to fall back to Python-pipeline names when the renderer-style file is absent. Multiplies the auto-populate code paths.

The HANDOFF §5c 'dual-path decisions' status reads 'Strict: omit all three (JS + Python + renderer heuristic). Leave room to build later.' This issue is the 'later' that needs a chosen direction, with the Phase E env-isolation work now in place.

Out of scope for Tier 5 Phase E. File for Tier 6+ planning.
close_reason: Phase B (renderer fallback) shipped in df08e1e with 19-test jest coverage and multi-client render verification (matt-wallmow zero warnings, mammoth-lakes correct fallback, p3realtync hybrid canonical-wins precedence). Phase A simplified to a one-time mammoth-lakes pagespeed migration (92cb9ce) after archaeology confirmed no active producer of split filenames. Three follow-up issues filed: 046 (fallback cleanup), ukr (latent build_audit.py reader bug), 1pq (missing GA4/GSC producer).

title: Write project SOP for AI-assisted feature/data additions (prevent dead-code-yet-tested pattern)
description: Prompted by Tier 5 audit finding: vaderSentiment-dependent sentiment analysis ran successfully (tests green post-aj1) but the renderer never displayed the output. aj1 fixed tests for unused code. Same pattern likely exists elsewhere. SOP should require: (1) every new analyzer/feature includes a documented renderer-consumer mapping; (2) tests must verify data reaches the report (not just that the analyzer runs); (3) dead-code purge cadence (e.g., quarterly grep for emit-but-never-read patterns); (4) checklist for AI assistants to follow when adding features. Plan toward writing this in Tier 5 or 6 once we have more example incidents to draw from. Source: bd memory + Tier 5 audit findings 2026-04-29.

title: Missing test/runtime deps: networkx + vaderSentiment cause 11 pytest failures
description: 11 pre-existing pytest failures across test_internal_linking.py (4 — missing networkx) and test_local_seo.py (7 — missing vaderSentiment). Analyzers use try/except-import and silently degrade to empty/zero when missing. Prod data-integrity implication: if build_audit.py runs in a venv missing these libs, extended internal-link metrics (density, betweenness, communities) and review sentiment are silently zero. Reports/XLSX/PPTX consumers see blank cells. Action: confirm prod venv has these (pip show networkx vaderSentiment in prod). If yes, add to pyproject.toml as optional extras + CI-only. If no, silent prod regression — add to main dependencies. Source: HANDOFF-POST-TIER-3 Section 5b.

title: Pre-commit max-kb cap conflicts with research-bundle reality
description:
rob-kittle's audit-data.json (2.0MB) and search-console.json (8.3MB) hit the 500KB pre-commit hook cap. The internalLinking section accounts for 1.3MB of audit-data.json (legitimate — site has 16K URLs); search-console.json's bulk is allQueries+allPages (full 24K queries, 25K pages). Both files were excluded from the rob-kittle onboarding commit (b733b28) since they're regenerable from the gather scripts.

Options:
1. Raise the pre-commit max-kb to e.g. 5000 (precedent: existing committed clients have files >500KB that pre-date the cap)
2. Trim allQueries/allPages in gather_search_console.py to top 1000 each (would reduce search-console.json from 8.3MB to ~700KB, still useful for offline analysis but better fits the cap)
3. Both 1 and 2

Decision needed before next large-site client onboarding.

title: populate-audit-data.js: brittle MD heading parsers for competitorComparison/contentCalendar/advantages
description:
scripts/populate-audit-data.js failed to parse three sections during rob-kittle audit:
- competitorComparison: 'could not parse Executive Comparison Table from competitor-analysis.md'
- contentCalendar: 'could not find Section 8 in FINAL-AUDIT-REPORT.md'
- advantages: 'could not find What [client] Does Better section in FINAL-AUDIT-REPORT.md'

The agents produce reports with valid content but use slightly different heading formats than the parser expects. Either: (a) make the parser more lenient (regex with multiple heading variants), (b) tighten the agent prompts to enforce exact heading text, or (c) move from MD-parsing to a structured handoff (agents emit JSON instead of MD).

title: No canonical GA4/GSC producer in /seo-audit workflow
description:
Of the 6 active clients, only p3realtync has canonical ga4-data.json + search-console.json. mammoth-lakes has split legacy files from a one-time 2026-03-19 import. matt-wallmow / laura-willis / liane-jamason / murray-gardner have neither canonical nor legacy GA4/GSC research files at all.

This means /seo-audit currently does not produce GA4 or Search Console research files for new clients — the data shows up only when manually imported. Result: the renderer's traffic + search-console pages render empty for most clients.

Scope: design and ship template/scripts/gather-ga4.js + gather-search-console.js mirroring gather-pagespeed.js, write canonical ga4-data.json + search-console.json. Wire into commands/seo-audit.md Step 5.5 next to the other gather-*.js invocations.

Out of i57 scope because i57 was about renderer/pipeline filename mismatch, not a missing producer altogether. Surfaced during i57 Phase A research.
close_reason: Producer-side ship verified end-to-end on rob-kittle (commits 7f5daed feat + 45047bb docs + b733b28 data). gather_ga4.py wrote ga4-data.json (5,311 sessions, 100 landing pages, 126 channels, 3 devices). gather_search_console.py wrote search-console.json (24,223 queries, 25,000 pages). Renderer log confirms canonical pickup: 'Auto-populated searchConsoleData: 50 queries, 50 pages' + 'Auto-populated trafficData: 8 channels, 3 devices, 25 pages'. Two side-fixes shipped along the way: 200ae60 (ClientContext empty-string filter) and e3fc35a (connector OAuth scope narrowing). North Star satisfied: GA4 + GSC are now part of /seo-audit Step 5.5, no manual data import needed for new audits.

title: Remove committed .collab/ directory (10 files incl 104KB binary collab.db)
description: Discovered during 0au v4 branch forensic investigation. The .collab/ directory (10 files) was committed in v4 at a139db9 and is currently tracked in site-audit-fixes-tier-4 (inherited). Contents: collab.db (104KB SQLite binary — runtime state artifact for a multi-LLM collaboration system), partner-prompt-claude.md, partner-prompt-codex.md, partner-prompt-gemini.md, partner-prompt.md, prompt-claude-diag.md, prompt-claude-impl.md, prompt-codex.md, prompt-gemini.md, prompt-orchestrator.md. The .md files are session-specific system prompts for the multi-LLM collab feature referenced in the v4 commit subject. The collab.db binary should have been blocked by the .gitignore *.db pattern but was committed while already tracked. Decision needed: (a) remove the entire .collab/ from git history and add .collab/ to .gitignore — these are session runtime artifacts not repo content, OR (b) keep the .md prompts if the collab system is intended to be checked in, but at minimum remove collab.db + gitignore it. CLAUDE.md §hard rules already lists .collab/ as working-tree noise (rule #5). Recommendation: git rm -r .collab/ + add .collab/ to .gitignore. Source: bd site-audit-fix-work-0au forensic.
close_reason: Resolved by chore: remove tracked .collab/ runtime artifacts. .gitignore line 19 already had .collab/, so prevention was in place; the 10 inherited tracked files are now removed via git rm. Verified empty git ls-files .collab/ post-commit.

description: Discovered during 0au v4 branch forensic investigation. Four .bak files are tracked in the repo from the v4 commit a139db9 ("feat: v4 — multi-LLM collab audit, retry logic, contentQuality permanent fix", 2026-04-15): template/reports/multipage/generate-multipage-report.js.bak, clients/laura-willis/reports/multipage/generate-multipage-report.js.bak, clients/liane-jamason/reports/multipage/generate-multipage-report.js.bak, clients/matt-wallmow/reports/multipage/generate-multipage-report.js.bak. The .gitignore covers clients/*/seo/research/*.json.bak and clients/*/seo/audit-data.json.bak but NOT generate-multipage-report.js.bak pattern — closing this issue should also add a gitignore entry to prevent recurrence. close_reason: Confirmed: git ls-files | grep '\.bak$' returns nothing. The 4 .bak files were already removed (likely during Tier 4 fix 14). .gitignore line 18 already covers *.js.bak so prevention is in place. Verified 2026-05-05.

title: Reliability sweep: 9 Python connectors bypass _request_sync retry coverage
description: Tier 2 Fix 6 added retry coverage to base._request_sync and routed DataForSEO _post through it. The other 9 sync connectors still call self.sync_client.request()/.post() directly with inline raise_for_status() — no retry coverage for transient failures. Files: connectors/{pagespeed,crux,business_profile,brand_mentions,social_audit,search_console,ga4,google_ads,local_seo}.py. pagespeed.py also has no rate-limit at all. Most natural fit: bundle opportunistically with whatever future fix touches any of these connectors. Source: HANDOFF-POST-TIER-3 Section 5a.

title: Calgary extract-text.js upstream-then-replace
description: Calgary's scripts/extract-text.js is a 275-line fork preserved through Tier 4 sync via sha256-fingerprint guard. Contains Calgary-specific community slugs + richer syllable algorithm + main/article extraction (vs template's body-wide approach). Owner needed: extract universally-useful improvements (syllable algo, main/article extraction) into template; remove Calgary-specific slugs from the fork (or move them to a config-driven mechanism); then sync calgary's extract-text.js. Bundle with whoever next touches extract-text.js or with Tier 5 Fix 16 if it touches the JS gather stack. Source: TIER-4-PLAN Q1.5 + Section 5 NEW item.

value: Spam classifier reframe SIMPLIFIES Fix 16 backlinks decision: with no classifier output needed, choose the path that just gathers and emits the raw list. May tilt other dual-path decisions where classifier complexity was a deciding factor. Per insight 2026-04-29.

Tier 5+ retired-code archive lives at /root/site-audit-retired/ (separate git repo, sibling to /root/site-audit/ and /root/site-audit-fix-work/). Mirror original paths inside (e.g., site-audit-retired/platform/src/audit_platform/analyzers/backlinks.py). Each retired file should include a header comment with: which tier retired it, what replaced it, why. Keeps main project clean + zero accidental-import risk + preserves optionality. Per user direction 2026-04-29.

Tier 5 spam classifier OMITTED entirely (strengthened from prior reframe). Not a manual-review warning UI either — just OMIT. Renderer's classification fallback heuristics also out. Reasoning: cannot say with absolute certainty that classifications are correct; classifier adds unnecessary complexity layer with false-positive liability. Per user direction 2026-04-29 (supersedes earlier 'reframe as warning' memory).

Tier 5 spam classifier reframe = drop classify-as-spam-or-not entirely. Surface manual-review WARNING with criteria (legit site, structure, ranking, age). Removes our liability for false-flagging legitimate domains. Same criteria seeds a future v2 classifier. Per user direction 2026-04-29.
PPC workflow (Fix 15) is OUT of Tier 5 scope. User building PPC separately to keep organic/PPC segregated and avoid tool wire-crossing. Per user direction 2026-04-29.

Tier 5 pre-commit safety = pre-commit framework (https://pre-commit.com) + .gitignore pattern clients/*/.env. Framework chosen over raw .git/hooks shell script for future-proofing. Per user direction 2026-05-03.

Tier 5 client .env segregation = TOP PRIORITY. Global .env for shared keys ONLY (template for copying, never read by connectors). On new-client creation, copy to clients/<c>/.env. Connectors read CLIENT-LOCAL .env, never global. Goal: zero cross-wire risk between clients (refund risk if Client A pulls Client B's GA4/GSC data). Per user direction 2026-04-29.

Tier 5 dual-path retirement = move to removed/ folder, not delete and not just @deprecated tags. Preserves optionality to learn from the loser or revert if the winner is worse. Per user direction 2026-04-29.

Tier 5 JS env-loading = custom lib/load-client-env.js helper (Option B). Reads clients/<slug>/.env via fs.readFileSync, parses KEY=value lines, returns object. Replaces process.env.X with env.X across ~10 gather scripts. Eliminates process.env cross-wire risk at language level. Per user direction 2026-05-03.
Tier 5 new-client onboarding = build /new-client skill that prompts for client keys and writes clients/<slug>/.env from global .env template. Confirmed scope item. Per user direction 2026-05-03.

Tier 5 Python env-loading = ClientContext class (Option C revised). Wraps pydantic Settings for validation; uses dotenv_values to parse without os.environ pollution. Carries slug + lazy .env load + audit_data_path() helpers. ~40 LOC new code. Per user direction 2026-05-03.

Project SOP needed for AI-assisted feature/data additions. Should prevent the dead-code-yet-tested pattern (sentiment analysis ran + tests passed but renderer never displayed it; aj1 made it green for nothing). SOP should require: every new analyzer/feature has a renderer consumer mapping + test that proves the data reaches the report; dead-code purges as part of routine hygiene. Plan toward writing this in Tier 5 or 6, not now. Per user direction 2026-04-29.

Tier 5 OVERRIDING PRINCIPLE: reliability, durability, consistency. Not simplicity. The audit pipeline must work every time. Choose paths with smallest failure surface, fewest false positives, most boring/well-tested patterns. Avoid cleverness. Per user direction 2026-04-29.
